signals.title: Record KRW 35T+ CapEx with 120T Yongin & P&T7 Packaging Plant
signals.signal: SK Hynix plans KRW 35T+ in CapEx for FY2026, up from KRW 29T in FY2025. The Yongin Semiconductor Cluster (originally KRW 120T, now expanded to KRW 600T) represents a multi-decade capital commitment. SK Hynix announced a $12.85 billion P&T7 advanced-packaging investment to expand HBM capacity for AI data centers. CapEx in 2026 is expected to increase significantly compared with 2025, with the majority allocated to infrastructure preparation centered on the Yongin Cluster and ramp up of M15X, and through the procurement of key equipment such as EUV tools.
key_points: SK Hynix plans KRW 35T+ in CapEx for FY2026, up from KRW 29T in FY2025.
SK hynix is investing 120 trillion won ($89 billion) in its Yongin cluster, targeting monthly DRAM production capacity of 1 million wafers by 2030.

SK Hynix reported a record quarterly profit on April 22, 2026, and announced a $12.85 billion investment in a new advanced-packaging plant with construction scheduled to start in April 2026, with wafer testing planned for October 2027.
This level of investment will consume virtually all free cash flow and potentially require debt financing.
signals.why_it_matters: Targeting monthly DRAM production capacity of 1 million wafers by 2030 requires massive infrastructure spend that locks in long-term competitive positioning in AI memory. The scale and timing directly enable SK Hynix to capture disproportionate share of the multi-year HBM supercycle, constraining competitors' ability to match capacity.
signals.chain_link: Upstream capex impacts equipment makers (ASML, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron) and materials suppliers (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, specialty gases), while downstream it enables customer fulfillment for hyperscalers (NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Meta) competing for AI compute dominance.
stakeholders: SK Hynix (capex financer and executor)
ASML, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron (equipment suppliers)
Shin-Etsu, SUMCO (wafer materials suppliers)
NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Meta (downstream HBM demand drivers)
Korean Development Bank (government financing)
signals.source: SK Hynix Q1 2026 Earnings + TrendForce, Seoul Economic Daily

signals.title: HBM4E Samples Shipped; 16-Layer 48GB at 16Gbps; 70% Rubin Allocation
signals.signal: SK hynix shipped samples of HBM4E, a next-generation DRAM for AI, to major customers, with the 12-layer HBM4E showing improvements in both performance and power efficiency. SK hynix showed off its next-gen 16-Hi HBM4 with 48GB, with 2TB/sec of memory bandwidth per stack, destined for NVIDIA's next-gen Vera Rubin AI platform, running at the industry's fastest speed of 11.7Gbps. UBS predicts that SK hynix will achieve approximately a 70% market share in the HBM4 market for NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin platform in 2026. In terms of revenue for the first quarter of 2026, SK Hynix firmly secured the top spot in the global HBM market with a 58% market share. On June 5, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang confirmed that SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron have all passed qualification and started production of HBM4 to supply NVIDIA's next-generation AI platform, Vera Rubin.
key_points: SK hynix shipped samples of 12-stack HBM4E with a maximum data processing speed of 16Gbps per pin and power efficiency that is up more than 20 percent from previous models.
The 16-Hi HBM4 48GB modules are destined for NVIDIA's next-gen Vera Rubin AI platform and run at the industry's fastest speed of 11.7Gbps.

UBS predicts SK hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in the HBM4 market for NVIDIA's Rubin platform in 2026, suggesting its current leadership is carrying over to future technology generations.
SK Hynix leads with approximately 50–55% market share, followed by Samsung at 35–40% and Micron at 5–10%, having been first to mass-produce HBM3E and secured the majority of NVIDIA supply contracts.
signals.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs forecasted that HBM demand for custom-ordered, ASIC-based AI chips will skyrocket by 82%, accounting for one-third of the market, and SK Hynix's early HBM4E qualification and planned 70% Rubin allocation locks in premium pricing and customer stickiness. This directly translates to revenue growth and operating margin expansion in 2026–27.
signals.chain_link: Secures downstream customer dominance (NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Meta ASICs) through next-generation technology leadership while maintaining premium pricing leverage over competing memory suppliers.
stakeholders: SK Hynix (technology leader & sole HBM4 ramp leader)
NVIDIA (primary HBM4 adopter for Rubin/Vera platforms)
Samsung, Micron (competing HBM suppliers losing share)
TSMC (advanced packaging partner for HBM4 base die)
Google, Amazon, Meta (ASIC customers demanding HBM4)
signals.source: SK Hynix Newsroom, CES 2026 coverage, TrendForce

signals.title: Multi-Year NVIDIA Partnership Announced June 2026; Vera Rubin/CPUs/RTX/Jetson
signals.signal: SK hynix and NVIDIA announce multi-year technology partnership for next generation memory aligned to NVIDIA's AI infrastructure roadmap. The agreement supports supply for advanced memory, addressing the extended development cycles, advanced fabrication and capital investments to sustain the global buildout of AI factories. SK hynix will diversify into new markets NVIDIA is creating — across AI infrastructure, personal AI and physical AI — developing memory for NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI supercomputers, Vera CPUs, RTX Spark-powered PCs and Jetson Thor robotics platforms. The two companies will apply AI to semiconductor chip design and manufacturing, using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo to accelerate semiconductor simulations, TCAD workflows and in-house engineering codes.
key_points: Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA, stated that advanced memory is essential to their performance and SK hynix has been an extraordinary partner to NVIDIA, playing a central role in delivering advanced memory technologies for NVIDIA AI computing platforms.
SK hynix will supply memory for Vera Rubin HBM for AI supercomputers, memory for RTX Spark desktop AI PCs, and memory for Jetson Thor modules that run humanoid and industrial robots.

The agreement builds on years of deep co-engineering collaboration that has powered some of the world's most advanced AI computing platforms and supports supply to address extended development cycles of advanced memory, enabling memory supply to keep pace with NVIDIA's infrastructure roadmap.
This deal ensures that NVIDIA gains greater influence over the hardware stack supporting its AI systems. SK hynix, meanwhile, gains a deeper role in one of the most important semiconductor markets.
signals.why_it_matters: Memory supply has become a constraint in AI hardware, with NVIDIA stating the shortage could last for quite a few years, and as AI models grow larger, memory moves more data and plays a bigger role in performance. The formalized multi-year partnership locks in preferred supplier status across NVIDIA's entire portfolio expansion (Vera, personal AI, robotics), protecting market share and enabling pricing power.
signals.chain_link: Directly anchors SK Hynix as NVIDIA's memory partner across AI infrastructure, edge, and physical AI platforms, foreclosing Samsung and Micron from competing for the largest customer relationships.
stakeholders: SK Hynix (long-term supply guarantor to NVIDIA)
NVIDIA (secures memory supply for all product lines)
Samsung, Micron (excluded from parts of NVIDIA roadmap)
TSMC (packaging co-development partner)
Google, Amazon, Meta (indirect beneficiaries via NVIDIA supply stability)
signals.source: NVIDIA Newsroom, SK Hynix Newsroom, TechTimes

signals.title: No-Price-Cap LTA Strategy; 20% HBM3E Price Hike for 2026; Margin Control
signals.signal: SK hynix is now adopting contracts that eliminate the industry-standard price cap, marking a departure from Micron's approach. Unlike traditional memory contracts where price ceilings are used to limit volatility, SK hynix's new structure allows spot market price increases to be fully reflected in contract pricing when supply shortages push market prices higher. Following reports that NVIDIA has been approved to sell its H200 AI chips to China, sources say Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026. ZDNet projects that Samsung and SK hynix could post NAND operating margins of 40-50% for the first half of 2026. Those margins are predicated not just on higher prices, but disciplined supply management and a willingness to walk away from unfavorable contracts.
key_points: SK hynix is adopting contracts that eliminate the industry-standard price cap, and may now be the only major memory supplier not applying a price cap in its long-term agreements.
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026, with HBM content per accelerator expected to increase by roughly 20–30% compared with earlier generations.

Samsung and SK hynix have begun moving away from long-term, fixed-price supply contracts, replacing them with shorter agreements and post-settlement pricing mechanisms. ZDNet projects SK hynix could post NAND operating margins of 40-50% for H1 2026.
Customers are prioritizing securing volume over pricing, which is sustaining the current pricing strength.
signals.why_it_matters: Removing price caps from long-term agreements enables SK Hynix to capture spot-market upside during structural HBM supply shortage, driving operating margin expansion from historical 20–30% to 50%+ in 2026–27. This directly flows to earnings and cash generation, supporting capex ambitions and shareholder returns.
signals.chain_link: Upstream suppliers (equipment, materials) face cost pressures but benefit from volume ramp; downstream customers (hyperscalers) face memory cost inflation but must accept it due to constrained supply.
stakeholders: SK Hynix (margin expander and price setter)
NVIDIA, Google, AWS, Meta (high-ASP memory buyers)
Samsung, Micron (pricing power competitors)
Apple, Intel, AMD (downstream customers accepting price hikes)
Investor base (valuation re-rating on margin expansion)
signals.source: TrendForce, Tom's Hardware, New Electronics, ZDNet

signals.title: Nasdaq ADR Listing July 10 2026; $29.4B Raise; Largest ADR Ever
signals.signal: In June 2026, SK hynix said it planned to raise up to US$29.4 billion through a Nasdaq listing of American depositary receipts, with proceeds intended for new semiconductor fabrication facilities in South Korea and chipmaking equipment to boost supply to fill the 2025–present global memory supply shortage. The factory push runs in parallel with SK Hynix's leap to the Nasdaq, set for July 10 under the ticker SKHY. The company is planning to issue American Depositary Receipts worth up to 45.45 trillion won (roughly $29.4 billion), with Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan serving as lead underwriters. If executed at that size, it would become the largest ADR listing in stock market history.
key_points: SK Hynix's Nasdaq leap is set for July 10 under the ticker SKHY, planning to issue American Depositary Receipts worth up to 45.45 trillion won (roughly $29.4 billion).
If executed at that size, it would become the largest ADR listing in stock market history.

On June 22, 2026, SK Hynix surpassed Samsung Electronics in market capitalization based on common shares, becoming the largest company on the KOSPI by market value. It marked the first time Samsung Electronics had relinquished its position as the KOSPI's most valuable listed company since November 2000, ending a reign of 25 years and 7 months.
Trading at an 8x forward P/E, the U.S. listing aims to re-rate its valuation against global peers, providing investors broader access to its essential AI supply chain role.
signals.why_it_matters: The Nasdaq listing simultaneously signals confidence in SK Hynix's market dominance, expands the global investor base, and raises capital for multi-year capex at a time when funding costs are favorable. The $29.4B proceeds directly fund Yongin and packaging expansion, de-risking capex execution and anchoring long-term supply capacity.
signals.chain_link: Provides capital funding for upstream equipment and materials orders; demonstrates to downstream customers (NVIDIA, Google, AWS) that capacity expansion is credible and funded.

signals.title: M15X Fab First Cleanroom May 2026; 20T Won Investment; HBM3E/4 Production
signals.signal: Infrastructure investment will continue expanding next year, including preparations for the Yongin Cluster 1 and the Advanced Package Plant in Indiana, USA. The company is boosting new capacity with M15X—whose cleanroom reportedly opened ahead of schedule and has begun equipment installation. SK hynix has started installing key equipment at its Cheongju M15X fab, which will produce HBM and other products. The company is set to complete the first clean room at its M15X fab in May 2026 and begin pilot operations. The facility, a key production hub with over 20 trillion won invested, will manufacture both HBM3E and HBM4. 10nm-class 6th-generation (1c) DRAM lines, intended for the upcoming HBM4E, will be introduced at the site.
key_points: SK hynix is set to complete the first clean room at its M15X fab in May 2026 and begin pilot operations, with the facility a key production hub with over 20 trillion won invested, will manufacture both HBM3E and HBM4.
M15X's cleanroom reportedly opened ahead of schedule and has begun equipment installation to produce HBM and other products.

SK hynix secured the world's first mass-production system for HBM4 last September, strengthened its packaging partnership with TSMC, built the Cheongju M15X fab, and established a dedicated HBM unit, a Global AI Research Center, and global production infrastructure. These moves position SK hynix to support both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale by 2026.
10nm-class 6th-generation (1c) DRAM lines, intended for the upcoming HBM4E, will be introduced at the site.
signals.why_it_matters: HBM3E will remain the dominant product this year, even as HBM4 ramps up, with estimates suggesting it will account for about two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, while HBM4 gradually gains traction. With NVIDIA launching its Blackwell Ultra accelerators and big tech players like Google and AWS expanding in-house ASIC-based AI chip development, HBM3E is increasingly being adopted as the memory of choice. M15X completion de-risks SK Hynix's ability to supply both HBM3E and HBM4 simultaneously, capturing demand across the product cycle.
signals.chain_link: Upstream: drives equipment and materials procurement (ASML, SUMCO, Shin-Etsu). Downstream: enables fulfillment of NVIDIA Blackwell/Rubin and Google/AWS custom AI chip HBM demand.

signals.title: Intel NAND SSD Acquisition Phase 1 Closed; Solidigm Enterprise SSDs
signals.signal: SK hynix closed the first phase of the transaction by acquiring Intel's SSD business and the Dalian NAND flash manufacturing facility in China. In exchange, SK hynix will pay US $7 billion in consideration. Solidigm will be headquartered in San Jose, California, and manage product development, manufacturing, and sales of the newly acquired SSD business. Lee Seok-hee, president and co-CEO of SK hynix will be appointed executive chairman of Solidigm. Rob Crooke, former senior vice president of Intel will be appointed CEO of Solidigm. SK Hynix is leveraging synergies with Solidigm, which has strength in high capacity QLC enterprise SSDs, to further strengthen competitiveness in addressing a wide range of customer needs in the AI data center and AI PC storage markets.
key_points: SK hynix closed the first phase of the transaction to acquire Intel's NAND and solid-state drive (SSD) business by acquiring Intel's SSD business and the Dalian NAND flash manufacturing facility in China for US $7 billion in consideration.

SK hynix sees the opportunity to greatly enhance its NAND Flash business competitiveness to the level of its world-leading DRAM business, as SK hynix excels in mobile NAND flash while Solidigm shows industry-leading strengths in enterprise SSDs (eSSDs). SK hynix will be able to take advantage of the synergy of the combined business portfolio.

SK Hynix is leveraging synergies with Solidigm, which has strength in high capacity QLC enterprise SSDs, to further strengthen competitiveness in addressing a wide range of customer needs in the AI data center and AI PC storage markets.

SK hynix will showcase SOCAMM2, a low-power memory module specialized for AI servers, and its lineup of 321-layer 2Tb QLC product, optimized for ultra-high capacity eSSDs, as demand surges from rapid expansion of AI data centers.
signals.why_it_matters: The Solidigm acquisition (Phase 1 closed April 2025) gives SK Hynix a fully integrated memory + storage solution for hyperscalers, enabling cross-selling and bundled offerings (HBM + DRAM + NAND SSDs) that lock in customer relationships and command premium bundled pricing, while also diversifying revenue beyond HBM alone.
signals.chain_link: Expands downstream product portfolio to serve complete AI data center infrastructure (memory + storage), reducing dependency on HBM pricing alone and enabling end-to-end customer solutions (Google, AWS, Meta).

signals.title: 2026 HBM Sold Out; LTA-Only Model with Google 5-Year Deal; Hoarding Controls
signals.signal: SK hynix announces its HBM volume for 2025 has sold out, with final negotiations with customers for HBM supply in 2026 coming soon. SK hynix has sold out most of its HBM memory chips for 2026, with 2025 supply exhausted. The company is finalizing 2026 sales discussions and expects HBM demand to rise sharply due to AI investments. SK hynix is pursuing a five-year long-term supply agreement with Google for commodity DRAM. SK hynix is also understood to be pursuing a five-year long-term supply agreement with Google for commodity DRAM. Memory manufacturers are tightening controls on customer orders. Micron, SK hynix and Samsung are said to be requesting greater transparency around end customers and order volumes, in an effort to prevent hoarding or overbooking that could further disrupt an already constrained market.
key_points: SK hynix announces its HBM volume for 2025 has sold out. SK hynix has sold out most of its HBM memory chips for 2026, with 2025 supply exhausted. The company is finalizing 2026 sales discussions and expects HBM demand to rise sharply due to AI investments.

SK hynix is pursuing a five-year long-term supply agreement with Google for commodity DRAM. Samsung and SK hynix are moving away from one-year, short-term contracts with global big techs, transitioning instead to an LTA-only model spanning three to five years. SK hynix is also understood to be pursuing a five-year long-term supply agreement with Google for commodity DRAM, with discussions also including extending the deal by an additional two years, contingent on next-generation HBM supply, as SK hynix is currently the primary supplier of HBM3E to Google.

Memory manufacturers are tightening controls on customer orders. Micron, SK hynix and Samsung are said to be requesting greater transparency around end customers and order volumes, in an effort to prevent hoarding or overbooking that could further disrupt an already constrained market.
Hyperscalers lock in future supply via multi‑year deals with Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, with much production already sold. HBM is sold out for 2026.
signals.why_it_matters: Fully sold-out 2026 HBM production and LTA-only customer model with hyperscalers locks in revenue visibility while preventing customer hoarding and excess inventory swings that would compress prices. Supply discipline combined with structural shortage creates sustained pricing power and margins.
signals.chain_link: Protects downstream customer relationships (Google, AWS, Meta) by ensuring transparent demand signals and priority allocation, while upstream suppliers (ASML, TSMC) gain visibility into multi-year equipment and packaging orders.
stakeholders: SK Hynix (supply gatekeeper and pricing setter)
Google, Amazon, Meta (locked-in LTA customers with allocation security)
Samsung, Micron (competing on LTA terms but with less leverage)
Secondary-tier customers (Broadcom, AMD, others facing allocation pressure)

signals.title: Former CEO Lee Seok-Hee Departs to Intel; Signals Talent & Knowledge Loss
signals.signal: Intel has appointed former SK Hynix and SK On chief executive Seok-Hee Lee as executive vice president of its contract chip-manufacturing business. Intel said Lee will report directly to CEO Lip-Bu Tan and oversee advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development and back-end manufacturing. Intel appointed former CEO of SK hynix and SK On Lee Seok-hee as a senior vice president in its foundry business, amid the US chipmaker's push into advanced semiconductor packaging. Intel announced that Lee will oversee advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development and back-end manufacturing at Intel Foundry. Prior to joining the battery maker, he served as chief executive of SK hynix, one of the world's largest memory chip manufacturers, where he played an instrumental role in developing and advancing the company's high-bandwidth memory.
key_points: Intel appointed former CEO of SK hynix and SK On Lee Seok-hee as a senior vice president in its foundry business. Lee will oversee advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development and back-end manufacturing at Intel Foundry and will report directly to CEO Lip-Bu Tan.

Prior to joining the battery maker, he served as chief executive of SK hynix, one of the world's largest memory chip manufacturers, where he played an instrumental role in developing and advancing the company's high-bandwidth memory.
Lee stepped down as chief executive of SK On at the end of May after 2 1/2 years in the role.
Lee also worked at Intel as an engineer from 2000 to 2010 before taking on leadership roles in South Korea.
signals.why_it_matters: The departure of a former SK Hynix CEO to Intel's advanced packaging division represents a loss of critical HBM and packaging expertise to a competitor. This elevates Intel's advanced packaging capabilities while creating organizational continuity risk at SK Hynix, though current CEO Kwak Noh-Jung remains stable. However, Lee's exit signals that Intel is making aggressive hires to catch up in packaging—a key constraint for HBM.
signals.chain_link: Upstream competitive dynamic: Intel's packaging hire may accelerate Intel's ability to compete in HBM4 packaging (a bottleneck), potentially reducing SK Hynix's packaging advantage over Samsung and Micron.
